name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.traceModelRepresentation_injective
title: Faithfulness of the representation on the CAR trace Hilbert space

content.display_title: Faithfulness of the representation on the CAR trace Hilbert space
content.one_sentence_role: Unitary conjugation preserves injectivity of the target-state representation.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra and $\tau$ its normalized trace. Fix a representative shell family and its chosen unitary links $L_j$ in the selected atomic representation $\pi$. Write $T=C^*(\pi(A),\{L_j\})$ for the resulting concrete target and $\iota:A\to T$, $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$, for its faithful unital source map. This fixes one target and one source map throughout. Let $(H_\phi,\rho_\phi,\xi_\phi)$ be the GNS representation of the chosen state extension $\phi$, and let $(H_\tau,\pi_\tau,\xi_\tau)$ be the CAR trace GNS representation. Choose once the pointed unitary $E:H_\tau\to H_\phi$ with $E\xi_\tau=\xi_\phi$ and $E\pi_\tau(a)=\rho_\phi(\iota(a))E$. Then $\widetilde\rho(t)=E^{-1}\rho_\phi(t)E$ is injective on $T$.
content.assumptions: The family, extension, and chosen unitary are the ones used to define `traceModelRepresentation`. Faithfulness of $\rho_\phi$ is the separately proved kernel-dichotomy result.
content.conclusion: The same concrete target admits a faithful representation on the nonzero separable space $H_\tau=L^2(A,\tau)$. Its restriction to $A$ is the CAR trace representation.
content.proof_summary: Undo the same conjugation and apply faithfulness of the original target-state representation.

proof_steps.text:
Suppose $\widetilde\rho(t)=\widetilde\rho(s)$. Since $E$ is a unitary onto $H_\phi$,

$$\rho_\phi(t)=E\widetilde\rho(t)E^{-1}=E\widetilde\rho(s)E^{-1}=\rho_\phi(s).$$

The theorem `tracialRepresentation_injective` then gives $t=s$. In the source this is the composition of the injective conjugation equivalence with the injective representation; it does not require another ideal argument.

content.lean_realization_notes: Injectivity concerns the homomorphism into operators, not a vector functional. The result does not assert irreducibility of this representation or norm separability of $T$. Conjugation uses the inverse on the left because $E$ points from the CAR space to the target-state space.
